readme_content:
# A crawler for Zig dependencies

generated a sqlite database of git repositories with zig dependencies.
Also includes a small web application to view the database contents.

Repositories are indexed from these sites if they have the topics
`zig` or `zig-package` assigned:

- <https://github.com>
- <https://gitlab.com>
- <https://codeberg.org>

Dependencies are resolved between those sites even if those topics
aren't set based on `build.zig.zon` urls.

Hosted on gitlab pages: <https://dasimmet.gitlab.io/zig-git-crawler/>

```bash
# build the exe
zig build
# setup an API token for github:
export GITHUB_API_AUTH_TOKEN=********************
# crawl through major all git hosting sites, create the db
zig build run
# query the db
sqlite3 zig-out/www/zig-git.db "SELECT * FROM view_manifest_tree"
# build the webapp:
zig build web
# run the dev webserver:
zig build dev
# open the browser to view it: http://localhost:8080/www
```

## TODO

### Web UI

- Needs quite a bit more explaining whats going on.
- Search for repositories in the main list
- Provide numerical indicators for dependencies and dependants
- Better and searchable selectors for `repo` and `ref` in the details view.
- The dependency/dependant queries have a depth field, however they
  don't take `path` dependencies into account since the sql query was
  easier to implement.

### Crawler

- Crawler is hitting Github/Codeberg API limits quickly and needs a
  few runs to populate.
- Github's Api is limited to 1000 search results. For now, I
  keep a list of search urls based on the repo creation date to
  work around it. Could be solved by calculating the URLs based
  on whats already in the DB.
- Crawler does not update the repository entries of dependencies, only
  those repos with `zig` and `zig-package` tags. New commits and
  manifests are fetched though.
- Between runs, the crawler relies on keeping the sqlite db file on the
  runner cache. Maybe it could be stored and downloaded to/from
  gitlab's package registry instead.
